column1: # Phigen's looks: a look's name, and after it a row that changes the
# theme for that look, written as data/theme.tsv writes one. The first
# is the one Phigen opens in. A look with nothing to change is the theme
# as it is. What each is called is data/text.tsv's: look.<name>.
# A look changes the ground, the inks and how much light there is; the
# light itself stays one colour. The two glass looks are Apple's Liquid
# Glass as Phiber wears it (phiber: theme/style/glass.rs): the window's
# ground lets the desktop show, blurred by the system (window.glass), and
# the window's panes, its bar and a panel that floats, blur what is
# behind them inside it (glass.*). Buttons, rows and icons are not glass.
# The Liquid Glass looks are Apple's as its own apps wear it (the
# Landmarks sample, BOT-anist's panels): clearer glass than the others,
# bending more at its rim and catching more light there, every part on
# a pane of it, and every corner rounder, the parts' and the modals'
# most of all. Its edge is a shine, thin and nearly the glass's own
# colour, not a border. Its text stands a point off the glass, a light
# under it (`text.shade`, `text.lift`), as on Vision Pro's panes.
